prs.title: Allow content mapper registrations to filter their files with an `include` glob, inherit default `extension` from manifest
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body:
Fixes #64362

## Limitations

Normally content mappers that specify `outputExtensions` participate fully in `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. As an example, the Ember content mapper registers `"outputExtensions": { ".gts": ".js" }` because an external build tool compiles `.gts` files to `.js` outputs. This controls two behaviors by TypeScript: (1) the declaration file output for a `Component.gts` file will be `Component.d.ts`, to correspond with the `Component.js` file produced by the external tool; and (2) the build will require `--rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` to be enabled so an import of

```ts
import Component from "./Component.gts";
```

can be rewritten as `import Component from "./Component.js"` in TypeScript's output. Dynamic imports like

```ts
await import(path + "/Component.gts");
```

also get routed through a helper that replaces the trailing `.gts` with `.js`.

This logic gets more complicated when a content mapper that uses `outputExtensions` also uses an `include` filter, because it's harder to tell, in a single-file emit context, whether the file resolved by a given import is governed by a content mapper registration that contributes a module specifier rewrite.

### Restrictions on imports affected by `rootDirs` and `moduleSuffixes`
